notes: national_crime_count figures are de-duplicated by persistent_id across forces; see each month's summary.json 'national' block for details. Check each entry's 'methodology' field before comparing months on a trend chart: 'full-force-boundary' means every force was queried using its real boundary that month; 'mixed' means at least one force (e.g. btp, which has no fixed geographic area) fell back to a 1-mile HQ-radius sample instead. A change in methodology between two months is a change in measurement approach, not necessarily a real change in crime. 'rolling_12mo_crime_count' sums the trailing window of up to 12 months (see 'rolling_window_months' for how many months actually went into it - it will be less than 12 near the start of the published history). See each month's full summary.json for country-level 'regions' breakdowns and per-category per-1000 rates, which aren't duplicated into this compact history file.
